# Results — Study 878 (Economic Policy Uncertainty)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Baker,
Bloom & Davis (2016): a newspaper-based **Economic Policy Uncertainty** index should predict
the future — (1) higher forward equity **volatility** (the vol story), and (2) higher forward
**returns** as compensation for bearing it (the risk-premium story). Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `d922d69b4b52` (the aligned monthly `[unc, spy, rv]` frame).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Signal source | **`vix_proxy`** — a documented, market-based proxy for policy uncertainty (**month-end ^VIX**, real yfinance tape). *The intended Baker-Bloom-Davis newspaper EPU feed (`policyuncertainty.com` / FRED `USEPUINDXM`) was **network-unreachable** from the build environment; rather than fabricate a series we fall back to a labelled proxy, following [387-economic-surprise-index](../../387-economic-surprise-index/)'s transparent-proxy discipline. VIX and EPU co-move (~0.4–0.6 in the literature) but VIX is market-implied, not text-based — this is a proxy, never the newspaper index.* |
| Real tape | SPY daily adjusted closes + ^VIX daily closes (yfinance, `auto_adjust=True`), cached under this study's own `_cache/`; **401 aligned months, 1993-02-28 → 2026-06-30** |
| Outcome A — forward vol | mean **annualised realized vol** over the next `H` months (SPY daily log-return std × √252, per calendar month) |
| Outcome B — forward return | `H`-month forward simple SPY return from the formation month-end |
| Predictor | the uncertainty **level** (and its month-over-month **change**), known at month-end `t`; the forward outcome is realised strictly after `t` (a built-in one-month execution lag) |
| Statistics | OLS with a **Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett, 6-lag)** *t* on the slope; R²; a block-shuffle placebo (1,000 draws); a two-era cut; a costed timer; a seeded synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** SPY is a single continuously-listed index ETF
(no cross-section, no delisting bias); the VIX proxy is a continuously-published index. The
material caveat here is **not** survivorship but **provenance**: the signal is a VIX proxy,
not the real newspaper EPU — the return-side conclusion (below) is where that matters least
(a null is a null), but the magnitudes on the vol side would differ for the text-based index.

## Leg 1 — forward realized vol on the uncertainty level (the "vol story")

| horizon | slope | HAC *t* | R² | β (per 1σ) | n |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | +0.00914 | **+10.21** | 0.507 | +0.71 | 400 |
| 3m | +0.00677 | **+9.44** | 0.388 | +0.62 | 398 |
| 6m | +0.00520 | **+7.41** | 0.301 | +0.55 | 395 |
| 12m | +0.00386 | **+6.48** | 0.231 | +0.48 | 389 |

The vol leg is **strongly significant at every horizon** (HAC *t* = +6.5 … +10.2, R² up to
0.51). On the *change* it survives too (*t* = +3.4 / +3.1 / +2.5 / +2.7). **But read it
honestly:** VIX *is itself* the market's forward-looking implied volatility, so "VIX predicts
realized vol" is close to **mechanical** — the well-known variance-risk-premium fact, not a
distinct nowcast, and it is a *coincident* stress reading rather than a directional edge.

## Leg 2 — forward SPY return on the uncertainty level (the "risk-premium story")

| horizon | slope | HAC *t* | R² | β (per 1σ) | n |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | +0.00032 | +0.65 | 0.003 | +0.06 | 400 |
| 3m | +0.00096 | +0.82 | 0.010 | +0.10 | 398 |
| 6m | +0.00181 | +1.24 | 0.017 | +0.13 | 395 |
| 12m | +0.00220 | +1.04 | 0.010 | +0.10 | 389 |

The risk-premium leg **fails**: not one horizon clears |*t*| = 2 (max +1.24 at 6m), R² ≈ 0.01,
and on the *change* it is weaker still (*t* = −0.49 … +0.86). High uncertainty simply does
**not** predict higher forward returns. The block-shuffle placebo agrees: the observed 3m
slope sits at **p = 0.258** (6m: p = 0.221) — indistinguishable from a broken-link null. (The
vol slope, by contrast, is **p = 0.000**.)

## Robustness — two eras (split 2009-01-01), horizon 3m

| era | RET *t* (slope) | RV *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1993 → 2008 (n=191) | **+0.09** (+0.00014) | +6.20 |
| 2009 → 2026 (n=210) | **+4.36** (+0.00336) | +8.18 |

The return leg's only sign of life is **post-2009** (*t* = +4.36) and it is **entirely absent
pre-2009** (*t* = +0.09). A relation that appears in one regime and vanishes in the other is a
**single-era artefact** — here the post-GFC QE/recovery drift (buying the dip during high-VIX
2009–2020 paid off), not a stable uncertainty premium. It fails the sub-era robustness bar.
The vol leg holds in both eras (mechanically).

## The timer — can you get paid for leaning into uncertainty?

Long/flat SPY, one-month lag, 10 bps one-way; "lean-in" holds SPY when uncertainty is in its
top tercile (the risk-premium bet), "de-risk" does the opposite.

| rule | net ann. | vol | Sharpe | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **lean-in** (risk-premium bet) | +5.9% | 11.9% | **0.49** | 0.36 |
| **de-risk** (avoid uncertainty) | +5.2% | 9.1% | **0.57** | 0.64 |
| **buy-and-hold SPY** | +11.4% | 14.8% | **0.77** | 1.00 |

**Neither** uncertainty-timed rule beats simply holding the index (Sharpe 0.49 / 0.57 vs
0.77); both give up return by sitting out. Turnover is low so costs barely bite — the rule
loses on *signal*, not friction. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded (spy, unc) world: the *previous* month's uncertainty drives *this*
month's vol (`edge_vol`) and drift (`edge_ret`). No network.

| world | ret_t (3m) | rv_t (3m) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge_ret = edge_vol = 0`) | +0.10 | +1.12 |
| planted (`edge_ret = 0.02`, `edge_vol = 0.6`, seed 878) | **+4.96** | **+14.26** |
| null, **10 seeds** | mean −0.41 (sd 1.20), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/10** | — |

The detector recovers *planted* forward relations on **both** legs cleanly and stays silent on
the null — so the real-tape return-leg null is a genuine absence of signal, not a dead
estimator. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited for the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The risk-premium claim — high policy uncertainty predicting *higher
  forward returns* — **does not hold**: HAC *t* = +0.65 … +1.24 across 1–12m (R² ≈ 0.01),
  placebo p = 0.258, and the lone post-2009 significance (*t* = +4.36) is **absent pre-2009**
  (*t* = +0.09), a single-era recovery-drift artefact. The vol leg is strongly significant
  (*t* ≈ +10) but **mechanical** — VIX *is* implied vol, so "it predicts realized vol" is a
  near-tautology and a *coincident* stress reading, not a forward edge. Net: uncertainty is
  contemporaneous, exactly the desk's prior. *Provenance: signal is a labelled **VIX proxy** —
  the real newspaper EPU feed was unreachable in-environment.*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No uncertainty-timed rule beats buy-and-hold (Sharpe 0.49 lean-in,
  0.57 de-risk, vs 0.77 for holding SPY); the timer loses on signal, not costs.
